subject: moth in computer relay
title: The First Computer Bug Was a Real Moth, and It's Still Taped in a Logbook

scenes.text: The first computer bug was an actual bug.
September 9, 1947. Harvard's Mark II, a relay calculator the size of a room, stops working properly.
The operators open panel F and find relay number 70 jammed. Inside: a moth.
They tape it into the logbook and write: first actual case of bug being found. Grace Hopper's team made the story famous.
The joke only works because bug already meant a fault. Edison was complaining about bugs in his circuits back in 1878.
The moth is still there, taped to the page, in the Smithsonian.

description:
The first computer bug ever logged was a real moth, found jammed in a relay of Harvard's Mark II in 1947.
On September 9, 1947, operators traced a fault to relay number 70 in panel F, pulled out a moth, taped it into the logbook and wrote First actual case of bug being found. The team included Grace Hopper, who made the story famous. The word bug already meant a mechanical fault: Thomas Edison used it in a letter in 1878. The logbook page, moth included, is in the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.
What's the weirdest cause of a tech failure you've ever seen?
